context_requirements: Expression of functional PPARG (highest in HEPG2 and MCF7 among these lines)
Presence of ABCC8/SUR1-Kir6.2 or SUR2-Kir6.1 KATP channels (not expected in most of these lines)
Insulin-secreting beta-cell phenotype for the canonical KATP-dependent mechanism (absent in all nine lines)
falsifiers: No change in PPARG target genes (e.g., FABP4, ADIPOQ, CD36, PDK4) at 24 h in HEPG2 or MCF7
Strong, reproducible transcriptional response at 6 h in any line, which would suggest an off-target or non-canonical rapid mechanism
Consistent upregulation of generic stress or apoptosis programs across multiple lines at 24 h
Dose-dependent changes in KATP-channel-related genes in lines lacking ABCC8/KCNJ11 expression

evidence.supports: Sulfonylureas such as glimepiride bind and agonize PPARG, altering PPARG target gene expression in adipocytes
Glibenclamide induces beta-cell apoptosis in human islets, but this requires beta-cell context absent from the nine lines
Sulfonylurea tolbutamide induces apoptosis in human islets via SUR1/Kir6.2-dependent mechanisms, again beta-cell specific
SUR1 is upregulated in capillary endothelial cells after brain injury, not a general feature of the tested cell lines
SUR1 mutations cause neonatal hyperinsulinism, confirming the canonical target is pancreatic beta-cell KATP channels

changes: Removed all late_down genes (CXCL2, IL1B, PTGS2, MMP1, MMP2, COL1A1, COL4A1, CCND1, MYC, EGR1, FOS, JUN, EDN1, SERPINE1): no cited abstract supports sulfonylurea-driven downregulation of these genes in the tested non-beta-cell lines; direction is unjustified.
Removed CEBPA from late_up: no cited abstract supports sulfonylurea-induced CEBPA upregulation; only PPARG agonism is supported.
Kept PPARG in late_up as the only justified transcriptional effect, based on PMID 15764598 showing sulfonylurea PPARG agonism and altered PPARG target gene expression.
Set generic_effects to 'none' because no cited abstract supports a generic proliferation or stress program in these lines.
Retained kinetics 'slow' and magnitude 'weak' as consistent with a nuclear-receptor-mediated PPARG effect rather than rapid KATP-channel signaling.
Retained line_response with weak effects only in HEPG2 and MCF7, reflecting PPARG expression, and none elsewhere; no cited abstract contradicts this.
Retained context_requirements and falsifiers as consistent with the beta-cell-specific canonical mechanism and the PPARG off-target mechanism.
Retained all five evidence citations because each abstract supports the stated claim about sulfonylurea biology.
